title: Persist the close usage record: docs/history/<feature>/usage.json + letter line
action: Persist the token-usage record at green close: write docs/history/<feature>/usage.json (detailed, per session) and append the one-line usage summary to the feature close letter in the human mailbox, with tests
description: Build on the close-usage-summary work already in close.rs (UsageBucket/CloseUsage, usage_session_ids, collect_close_usage, close_usage_line). (1) Extend collect_close_usage (or add a sibling) so the per-session Rollup detail is kept, not only the summed buckets: for each counted session keep {session_id, models, subagent_models, subagent_count, started_ms, ended_ms, totals:{new,cached,total}}. (2) On the GREEN, non-dry-run close path, after usage is computed, write docs/history/<feature>/usage.json with write_text_atomic (same precedent as promote-proposals.md): pretty JSON {schema: "bee-usage/v1", feature, closed_at (ISO), sessions: [per-session detail], skipped, totals: {main:{new,cached,total}, subagents:{new,cached,total}, total:{new,cached,total}}}. Write the file on every green close, even when sessions is empty and only skipped is nonzero — an empty record with a skipped count and a missing file must not read alike. Give the write the same bookkeeping/auto-commit treatment promote-proposals.md gets (follow the existing precedent in close.rs; if the auto-commit is path-scoped to .bee only and does not cover docs/history, leave the file uncommitted exactly as promote-proposals is left, and say so in the cap report). (3) Append the close_usage_line text to the feature close letter the mailbox gets at close (record_feature_close_in_mailbox path — the letter composer may live in close.rs or verbs/mailbox.rs; follow where the letter body is built), only when a usage line was rendered. (4) Tests beside the existing close usage tests: green-close fixture asserts usage.json exists with the right sessions/skipped/totals numbers and schema field; a zero-readable-transcript fixture asserts the file is still written with sessions [] and the skipped count; the letter test asserts the usage line lands in the letter body when present. Follow existing test style.
acceptance: A green bee close writes docs/history/<feature>/usage.json with per-session model/subagent detail and feature totals (empty-but-skipped recorded too), and the close letter carries the usage line; scoped cargo tests green.
judge_obligation_ack: touches close.rs and mailbox.rs only — no hook-guard source; hooks/ not in files

trace.outcome: Green close writes docs/history/<feature>/usage.json with per-session detail and feature totals; the close letter carries the usage line

Put the usage line in its own Token usage letter section rather than under Usage — that section lists the docs a human opens to use the thing, and a token count is a different question — found a better route
